================================================================================
OBELISK SET THEORY PROVER — CANONICAL UNAMBIGUOUS NOTATION SPECIFICATION
================================================================================
Repository: set_theory_prover (Variant 1 = MKTD1 & Variant 2 = MKTD2)
Purpose:    Unambiguous distinction between logical formulas in Variant 1 (MKTD1),
            constructive types/functions in Variant 2 (MKTD2), and computation-level
            boolean truth values (Bool), across all three printing strategies:
              (x.1) LaTeX
              (x.2) Unicode
              (x.3) Plain-text ASCII-only textual concrete syntax

3) Separate Notation for Boolean Values (Bool : Type)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Question: "Also do we need a separate notation for boolean values or not?"
Answer:   YES — a separate notation for boolean values (b : Bool) is strictly
          necessary to eliminate ambiguity between three distinct layers:
            (i)   Syntactic formulas of the object theory (T / F, ⊤ / ⊥, \top / \bot : Fm)
                  in Variant 1, which are syntactic AST objects proved by sequents;
            (ii)  Constructive types (Unit / Void, 𝟙 / 𝟘, \mathbf{1} / \mathbf{0} : Type)
                  in Variant 2, which are inhabited by proof/program terms; and
            (iii) Boolean data values (true / false : Bool), which are the two
                  canonical term inhabitants of the two-element computation type
                  Bool (UBool in typetheory.ML), passed as arguments to polymorphic
                  conditionals simple_if(T_e, b, t_1, t_2), dependent conditionals
                  if_dep(T_e, b, t_1, t_2) with T_e : Bool -> Type (selecting
                  branch types T_e(true) and T_e(false)), and decidable SML/kernel
                  boolean side-conditions (isFree, FFI, NFV, Ctx_eq).

1.1 Latex

\mathsf{false}                    (Boolean falsity value: false : \mathsf{Bool})
\mathsf{true}                     (Boolean truth value: true : \mathsf{Bool})
\mathsf{Bool}                     (Two-element Boolean computation type, UBool)
\neg_{\mathsf{b}}, \land_{\mathsf{b}}, \lor_{\mathsf{b}} (Boolean negation, conjunction, disjunction on \mathsf{Bool})
\mathsf{simple\_if}(T_e, b, t_1, t_2) (Polymorphic conditional over T_e : \mathsf{Type}, b : \mathsf{Bool})
\mathsf{if}_{\mathsf{dep}}(T_e, b, t_1, t_2) (Dependent conditional over T_e : \mathsf{Bool} \rightarrow \mathsf{Type}, b : \mathsf{Bool})


1.2 Unicode

𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲       (or false : Bool)     (U+1D5F3.. / ASCII word token: Boolean falsity value of type Bool)
𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗲        (or true : Bool)      (U+1D601.. / ASCII word token: Boolean truth value of type Bool)
Bool                              (Two-element Boolean computation type, UBool)
¬ᵦ, ∧ᵦ, ∨ᵦ                        (Boolean negation, conjunction, disjunction on Bool)
simple_if(Tₑ, b, t₁, t₂)          (Polymorphic conditional: simple_if(Tₑ, true, t₁, t₂) = t₁, simple_if(Tₑ, false, t₁, t₂) = t₂)
if_dep(Tₑ, b, t₁, t₂)             (Dependent conditional over Tₑ : Bool → Type: Tₑ(true) → Tₑ(false) → Tₑ(b))


1.3 Unambiguous syntax (Plain-text ASCII-only textual concrete syntax)

false                             (Boolean falsity value: false : Bool)
true                              (Boolean truth value: true : Bool)
Bool                              (Two-element Boolean computation type, UBool)
not_b, and_b, or_b                (Boolean negation, conjunction, disjunction on Bool)
simple_if(T_e, b, t1, t2)         (Polymorphic conditional over T_e : Type, b : Bool)
if_dep(T_e, b, t1, t2)            (Dependent conditional over T_e : Bool -> Type, b : Bool)
